channel.title: System Nīti — A Field Manual for Resilient Systems
channel.description: Sixteen sutras and one decree, restated from Chanakya for engineers. A field manual for designing resilient systems — built for those who rule small republics of services.

item.title: Sutra 01 — The Throne: A system without clear intent is fragile
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: The first sutra — on the three questions every system must answer before a single line is written. Includes real-world case studies (Knight Capital, Healthcare.gov) and the operating cadence that keeps the throne defended.
item.content:encoded:
The kingdom rises or falls in the moment the throne is set. Not in the year of coronation. Not in the decade of consolidation. In the moment.

Every system, before its first commit, must be able to answer three questions: Why are we building this? What does success look like? What is the failure mode we must survive?

This essay is the full deep-dive on the first sutra — with the test, the cadence, and the case studies that show what happens when the throne is undefined.

Read the full essay →

item.title: Sutra 02 — The Fort: Build the fort before you invite the market
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Architecture is not aesthetic. It is survival planning — a document of what you have already agreed to defend. Forthcoming — the long-form deep-dive on architectural boundaries, data models, and the discipline of a one-page diagram.

item.title: Sutra 03 — The Treasury: Extravagance is the first ruin of kings
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Resources are your treasury — finite, precious, accountable. Forthcoming — capacity planning, cost as a first-class constraint, throttling and quotas.

item.title: Sutra 04 — The Spies: Spies are the eyes of the king
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Telemetry is the mind of the system. Forthcoming — metrics, logs, traces, SLOs, error budgets, dashboards that earn their place.

item.title: Sutra 05 — The Ministers: A throne without loyal ministers is bare
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Design for teams as much as you design for code. Forthcoming — service ownership, on-call, code review, the org-chart / architecture-chart alignment.

item.title: Sutra 06 — The Borders: Promises bind the weak; contracts bind the strong
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: APIs are borders between polities. Forthcoming — contract-first design, versioning, defensive design, idempotency, the discipline of stable interfaces.

item.title: Sutra 07 — The Armies: Armies that cannot coordinate lose battles
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Horizontal scaling first. Stateless services where possible. Forthcoming — sharding strategies, consistent hashing, re-sharding, capacity planning at scale.

item.title: Sutra 08 — The Trade: Trade-offs are the currency of rulers
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Caching is the art of buying speed with the coin of consistency. Forthcoming — cache patterns, invalidation, consistency models, the saga pattern.

item.title: Sutra 09 — The Gate: When the battering-ram approaches
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Expect failures — design for them. Forthcoming — circuit breakers, bulkheads, backpressure, retries with jitter, graceful degradation.

item.title: Sutra 10 — The Records: A king without records forgets his lineage
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: RPO and RTO are promises to the kingdom. Forthcoming — backup strategies, restore drills, schema migrations, the discipline of testing recovery.

item.title: Sutra 11 — The Watch: An open gate invites invasion
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Principle of least privilege. Threat model early. Forthcoming — IAM, mTLS, encryption, secret management, incident response.

item.title: Sutra 12 — The Coronation: A wise king does not burn the city with each celebration
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Canary releases. Blue-green. Feature flags. Forthcoming — progressive delivery, infrastructure as code, post-deploy verification, rollback discipline.

item.title: Sutra 13 — The Trial: As soon as the fear approaches, attack and destroy it
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Chaos engineering is you bringing fear close, so you learn to destroy it on your terms. Forthcoming — fault injection, game days, blast radius, runbook-driven experiments.

item.title: Sutra 14 — The Library: If knowledge dies with the king, the realm enters anarchy
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Living docs. Onboarding as part of code quality. Forthcoming — system overviews, runbooks, the two-week onboarding test, documentation as architecture.

item.title: Sutra 15 — The Council: Not knowledge alone, nor force alone
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: Balance autonomy with platform conventions. Forthcoming — standards without blockade, cost attribution, ethics, the governance cadence.

item.title: The Decree — Ten steps to a resilient realm
item.author: veers@veers.me (Veer)
item.description: The operating procedure that compresses the fifteen sutras into ten steps. Forthcoming — the weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual practices that keep the doctrine alive in a system whose people will, eventually, change.
